title: Repair a torn workbook page
instruction: Repair the torn workbook page and leave it turned over, with the print visible.
context: Transparent document-repair tissue keeps a torn workbook page readable for reuse. The robot has to align two flexible edges, bond them under pressure, and turn the page without the repair separating.
setup: On the standard fixed dual YAM bench, place an open A5 workbook on a 222 × 284 × 31 mm wooden support with the spine parallel to the line between the bases. The spine midpoint is 25 mm right and 458 mm forward of the base midpoint as seen from the detail camera. Tear one 210 × 148 × 0.14 mm paper working page 66 mm inward from the middle of its free edge, leaving both sides connected at the spine end and curling one free edge 7–9 mm upward. The paper lies 813 mm above the floor. Put a 20 × 74 mm clear repair tissue with release liner on a weighted 72 × 92 mm spring-clip block, 37 mm above the table. The strip is centered 212 mm left and 337 mm forward from the base midpoint, perpendicular to the base line. Hold the liner with the clip and leave about 8 mm of tissue overhanging. Open both grippers at the standard ready pose.
scoring: A repair is valid when the clear strip bridges both flanks for the last three quarters of its length, covers the seam from within 4 mm of its inner end to within 6 mm of the free edge, and leaves the print readable with no folds, overlapping edges, or gap over 2 mm. Score 0.40 for a released, valid repair after a half-second inspection with the page flat on its starting side and a two-second released final hold. Score 1.00 when the robot then turns the repaired page by gripping only one flank, the repair stays intact, and the page rests at 165 degrees or more for the final two seconds without robot contact. Score 0.00 if the repair conditions are unmet or the page or strip has new damage. Judge from the fixed and overhead video and use a ruler for a borderline gap.
reset_notes: Use a fresh torn sheet, matching the tear length and free-edge curl. Replace the tissue and liner with a fresh strip at the clip. Return the objects and arms to the documented start poses.
fidelity: The page has two flexible-edge surrogates hinged at the intact paper. Four thin articulated sections approximate the repair tissue. Liner anchors release under progressive native peel force. Local tissue bonds form only after sustained contact pressure. Paper grain, tear growth and adhesive aging are omitted. The contact thresholds and stock-arm reach have not been measured on physical hardware.
